source.title: Sparse Autoencoders Work on Attention Layer Outputs

record.file_problem: The supplied post is readable and complete as presented; it refers to an external appendix that is not included.
record.tranche_reason: The post extends SAE feature analysis to attention-layer outputs and reports results about those features. It does not test the toy-model geometry or capacity account in the claim.
record.gate_note: The post reports its own SAE feature analyses, including interpretability and dead-feature estimates, and measures how selected features relate to activations and downstream computation. Its discussion of attention-head superposition is cautious; head-level distribution results are recorded under fits_no_version. The post also cites findings from other work, which are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: Trains an SAE on attention-layer outputs of a real-text two-layer LM (gelu-2l), a new setting. It reports whether sparse, interpretable, causally relevant features are recovered (V4) and where the dictionary falls short of complete or clean units (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is essentially right. The authors conclude that attention-output SAEs learn sparse, interpretable features usable for circuit analysis. They also report nontrivial polysemanticity at low activations and say the evidence does not settle whether the 'Which' feature is attention-head superposition. They add that a large per-token induction family suggests very wide SAEs may be needed, and that L1H6 shows attention-head polysemanticity.
record.recipe_differences: The post says it replicates Anthropic's MLP SAE work on attention outputs, using concatenated z vectors across heads from the final layer of gelu-2l rather than MLP activations. It also investigates head contributions and upstream circuits.
record.method_sensitivity: The post reports more polysemanticity in lower activation ranges; it also notes that results depend on feature/context proxies that were imperfect.

fits_no_version.finding: Some attention SAE features draw on multiple heads, while others are explained by roughly one head. The authors leave open whether this is attention-head superposition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention-layer SAE features can be distributed across several attention heads (possible head superposition).

fits_no_version.finding: Ablating L1H6 turns off 443/450 induction features. It also raises loss on non-induction code features more than ablating a control head does.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Individual attention heads are polysemantic, serving several distinct SAE-identified roles.

record.problems: The study uses one two-layer model and a 16384-wide SAE; the authors estimate 24% of features are dead and acknowledge polysemanticity, especially at low activations. Feature interpretations are partly based on shallow inspections and imperfect proxies; the board-feature proxy correlation is 0.50. The authors say the attention-head-superposition case study is not clean enough to settle the interpretation. Some detailed analyses are in an external appendix not included in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results were omitted.

untested.parts: Stability across seeds or training runs, and canonicality across dictionary sizes, are not tested.
LLM-scale models and feature spreading across MLP neurons are not tested. The setting is attention outputs of a two-layer model only.
Neuron polysemanticity is not tested; only attention-head polysemanticity is reported.

missing.what: SAE reconstruction quality: average L0 ~12 and ~87% loss recovered
The 'token is next by induction' family is ~5% of living features. The authors say it implies an SAE at least ~50k wide, while this one is 16k, so the dictionary is incomplete.
The authors suspect unrecovered true features appear as linear combinations of learned features because the SAE is too small.
Variance explained by 'board' source tokens rises with activation threshold, reaching >99.9% at threshold 5, so polysemanticity is concentrated in low activations.
missing.locator: Understanding how the feature is computed

record.verdict_notes: Informal two-week MATS sprint post on the Alignment Forum, with one small model and no uncertainty estimates. The interpretability estimate rests on shallow inspection of 50 features. I treated gelu-2l as a real-text LM for V4 (as for Bricken et al.'s one-layer model), while noting it is not LLM-scale.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test overcomplete toy networks storing sparse features as nearly orthogonal overlapping directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular geometry.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
It reports polysemanticity of an attention head, not polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of neuron polysemanticity.
The model is a two-layer language model, not an LLM-scale model; the post does not test feature spreading across neurons in LLMs.

The post examines interpretability and some functional validity of SAE features, but does not test stability across training runs or whether features are canonical units. Its feature-coverage estimates are limited and do not establish completeness.
Does not test whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional features.

rows.operation_detail: Estimated interpretability among the alive features in the first 50 inspected.

relation.reason: Its own measurements test sparse feature recovery under V4, and its observed polysemanticity and incompleteness argument bear on V5.

tranche.reason: Extends SAE feature recovery to concatenated attention-head z outputs in gelu-2l and reports interpretability and causal results in that new setting.

source_check.notes: Several printed table differences are arithmetically inconsistent with their accompanying means; R12–R14 reproduce the source correctly. The interpretability estimate is shallow, and the authors explicitly leave attention-head superposition unresolved.

reader_labels.condition: gelu-2l attention-output SAE; inspected feature sample and selected feature analyses
reader_labels.reason: The post reports dead features, only an estimated 82% interpretability among alive features in the first 50, and imperfect proxy alignment for a studied feature; these findings do not support treating the dictionary as fully complete or uniformly interpretable (R1-R5).
